The battery has e.m.f. 9 V and negligible internal resistance.
What is the maximum range of the output voltage?
A
0–2 V
B
0–5 V
C
2–3 V
D
2–5 V

hints: Notice one output terminal is fixed at the left of the $2 \Omega$ resistor and the other is the slider on the $3 \Omega$ resistor, so the output spans the $2 \Omega$ resistor plus part of the $3 \Omega$ resistor.
Find the series current from the $9 \text{ V}$ battery and the total $2+3+4 = 9 \Omega$ resistance, then use $V = IR$ for the $2 \Omega$ and $3 \Omega$ sections.
Compare the output when the slider is at the left end of the $3 \Omega$ resistor with when it is at the right end to get the minimum and maximum voltages.
walkthrough: The $2 \Omega$, $3 \Omega$ and $4 \Omega$ resistors are in series across the $9 \text{ V}$ battery, so total resistance is $R = 2+3+4 = 9 \Omega$.
With negligible internal resistance, the series current is $I = V/R = 9/9 = 1.0 \text{ A}$.
Voltage across the fixed $2 \Omega$ resistor is $V = IR = 1.0 \times 2 = 2 \text{ V}$, and voltage across the whole $3 \Omega$ potentiometer is $1.0 \times 3 = 3 \text{ V}$.
When the slider is at the left end of the $3 \Omega$ resistor, the output includes only the $2 \Omega$ drop, so $V_{min} = 2 \text{ V}$.
When the slider is at the right end of the $3 \Omega$ resistor, the output includes both drops, so $V_{max} = 2 \text{ V} + 3 \text{ V} = 5 \text{ V}$.
The output can therefore vary continuously from $2 \text{ V}$ to $5 \text{ V}$. This is option D.

A.explanation: This gives only the $2 \text{ V}$ across the $2 \Omega$ resistor and ignores the extra $0$ to $3 \text{ V}$ added as the slider moves along the $3 \Omega$ resistor.

B.explanation: This assumes the output can fall to zero, but one output lead is fixed after the $2 \Omega$ resistor so at least the $2 \text{ V}$ drop across it is always included.

C.explanation: This gives only the $3 \text{ V}$ variation along the potentiometer and omits the fixed $2 \text{ V}$ from the $2 \Omega$ resistor in series.

D.explanation: The output always includes $2 \text{ V}$ across the $2 \Omega$ resistor plus $0$ to $3 \text{ V}$ from the slider position, giving $2 \text{ V}$ to $5 \text{ V}$.
